title: Salt and Spire
premise: Jonah Hartwell, youngest and least valued member of the Guild of Impossible Things, keeps its ledgers in a free city slowly being strangled by the usurper's armies. When a dying courier presses a salt-stained map into their hands, Jonah learns the guild's founder sold a soul—Jonah's own—to the court beneath the mountain generations ago, and that the map is the only key to reclaiming it. Hunted by guild elders who want the secret buried and by the usurper's soul-brokers who want it found, Jonah descends into the mountain court with an unlikely band: a disgraced guild archivist, a deserter soldier, and the stranger's vengeful daughter. In the end Jonah confronts the founder's ghost at the seat of the debt, chooses to pay the price of survival rather than pass it on, and shatters the inheritance of souls—returning to the free cities not as invisible, but as the one who ended the trade.
about_author: Petra Zhou is a former shipping clerk who spent years cataloguing other people's debts before turning to fiction about what we owe. She writes from a coastal apartment full of maps, most of them wrong on purpose.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. In the besieged free city of Vell, Jonah balances the guild's accounts of impossible trades while elder Master Corvane dismisses them as bookkeeping, not magic. A dying courier collapses in the counting-house and presses a salt-stained map into Jonah's hands with a warning. Emotional beat: quiet resentment curdling into fear as Jonah realizes they've been seen holding something dangerous.

chapters.title: What the Founder Sold
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Hiding in the guild archives, disgraced archivist Sable Ives deciphers the map: it leads to the court beneath the mountain, where the guild's founder pawned a soul to buy the guild's survival—a soul bound by bloodline to Jonah. Corvane demands the map be burned. Emotional beat: the vertigo of discovering your life was collateral in someone else's bargain.

chapters.title: Salt on the Doorstep
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. The usurper's soul-brokers raid Vell hunting the map; Corvane betrays Jonah's location to save the guild's charter. Jonah flees with Sable and meets Wren Ashfall, the dead courier's daughter, who has tracked the map for years. Emotional beat: grief and guilt—Jonah survives because others don't.

chapters.title: The Deserter's Road
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Fleeing east, the trio is caught by Tam, a deserter from the usurper's armies who knows the mountain passes—and knows what happens to souls the brokers collect. He bargains his knowledge for passage away from the war. Emotional beat: wary trust forged between people who have all been spent like currency.

chapters.title: The Market of Borrowed Breath
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. In the neutral waystation city of Ondrel, the group must trade an impossible thing for supplies and discover the soul-trade's reach: brokers auction fragments of the desperate. Jonah witnesses a sale up close and nearly sells the map. Emotional beat: horror at realizing the market would price them kindly, and resolve hardening in response.

chapters.title: Corvane's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Corvane catches up, offering Jonah amnesty if the map is surrendered—the guild will simply sell Jonah's soul back on installment, as tradition allows. Sable reveals she once helped falsify such ledgers and refuses to let history repeat. Emotional beat: the seduction of a fair-sounding deal, and the courage to refuse an inheritance of debt.

chapters.title: Under the Mountain
chapters.summary: POV Tam. Guided by Tam through abandoned mine-shafts, the four slip past the usurper's siege lines into the roots of the mountain, where the air tastes of salt and old promises. They find the door the map marks—and the bones of everyone who ever tried to knock. Emotional beat: dread giving way to grim determination at the threshold.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. In the candlelit court, the Steward of Debts offers Jonah a choice: reclaim their soul by transferring the debt to another living heir—or leave it, safe but owned. Jonah discovers the founder's ghost still lingers, unrepentant, insisting survival justifies everything. Emotional beat: fury and pity entwined as Jonah faces the ancestor who made them currency.

chapters.title: Spirefall
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Refusing every offered transfer, Jonah burns the original contract in the court's ledger-flame, shattering the spire's claim—but the collapse threatens to bury them all. Tam holds the passage, Sable carries the wounded, and Wren drags Jonah out as the mountain exhales centuries of stolen breath. Emotional beat: sacrifice without martyrdom; the price paid is the inheritance itself.

chapters.title: A New Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Weeks later, the usurper's advance stalls as soul-brokers lose their leverage; Vell begins to breathe again. Jonah reopens the guild's ledgers under new rules—nothing traded that isn't freely given—with Sable, Tam, and Wren beside them. Emotional beat: belonging earned rather than inherited, and the quiet joy of writing the first honest entry.
